sections.title: TRAINING
sections.html:
• Interns

  • For training an intern, the trainer should not work side-by-side with the intern the entire time. Instead, this is the training pattern to be used:
  1. Train verbally on the next item in his/her sequence
  2. Show intern how to do it once
  3. Watch the intern do it on his/her own
  4. Once you're satisfied the intern understands and can do it on his/her own, go work on your project
  5. When the intern reports to you that he/she is ready for his/her next item in his/her sequence, review the work on the previous item, and once you're satisfied the quality is good and all his/her questions are answered, move on to the next item and repeat this pattern.

sections.title: TIME MANAGEMENT
sections.html:
• Punctuality

  • On-time!

  • We define on time as early. If you clock-in at 8:01, you are late if your shift starts at 8.
  • If scheduled to open the store, please clock in 10 minutes early to allow for opening procedures and guest readiness by 10:00 sharp.

  • Late

  • If you are running late, please text your direct supervisor.

  • Morning Meeting

  • 7:55 Pre-Meeting Convo
  • 8:00 Morning Meeting (led by Brigham or member of BLP Leadership Team) as assigned
  • Professional Standards & Team Culture (one bullet point per day)
  • Introduce New Team Members OR Ask for ONE person to share “Good News”
  • Brigham Reminders or Quick New Training
  • Shop Manager Reminders or Quick New Training
  • QUEUE Reminder - Anyone who has questions, needs help or training, please talk to your direct manager immediately after the morning meeting to make specific requests which will then be prioritized by the manager to plan how to get you the support you need!

  • Productivity

  • Limit personal conversations & “hanging out”
  • When working, time should be focused on work tasks

  • Phones

  • Texting

  • No texting or personal calls
  • Please text and chat only during breaks

  • Videos

  • No video watching during paid work time unless approved BLP training videos specific to requested training time or current assigned work project
  • No videos playing of podcasts

  • Listening

  • YES! Listen while you work... audio only, no video and with personal headphones.
  • Please use headphones in break room for all audio

  • Breaks

  • Lunch breaks would be for shifts longer than 4 hours.
  • If needed, take a 15 minute paid break per 4 hour shift.
  • For example: if you’d like to have a paid 30 minute lunch, then don’t take either 15 minute break.
  • Or if you’d like to enjoy 2 paid 15 minute breaks, then clock out for your lunch.

  • Overtime / Work Hours

  • Limit your work hours to 20 (part-time) or 40 (full-time) unless prior authorization has been granted for overtime work. If you accidentally or purposefully work extra hours one day or week, then cut your day or week short the following day or week so that your overall work hours balance out to the correct number of hours worked.
  • For example, if you normally work 8-4 and you have a big project to finish for a deadline and so you work until 6 two days in a row, then leave 4 hours early that Friday, unless you have been approved for overtime hours.
  • Discuss any overtime concerns or questions with your direct supervisor.

  • Time Off

  • Time off is non-paid.
  • To ask for time off, talk to your direct supervisor (not admin) to get time approved.
  • Once approved make sure it is added to your BLP calendar.
  • For field technicians please send a quick text to admin after time is approved so that we can make sure to reschedule any tunings

  • Clocking In/Out (video)

  • When you arrive at 8am you'll clock in to the first piano you intend to work on. If you take a break, just stay clocked into the piano you were working on. If you change midday to a different piano, then clock into that next piano. When you do Friday cleaning from 3:30-4:00, just stay clocked in the last piano you were working on before cleaning. If you get called away from your piano work for 1-29 minutes for some random tasks, just stay clocked into the main piano you are working on. If you are going to be doing a non-piano work task (like go help the movers as a third guy for a few hours) for 30+ minutes, then do a detailed time punch to "misc". Otherwise, you will always be clocked into a specific piano you are currently working on. Any questions, please text the front desk at 801-701-0113.

sections.title: SAFETY (Intro Video)
sections.html:
Help everyone prevent shop accidents and injuries by reminding each other of safety precautions for loose clothing, hair tied back and no jewelry. Employees are also encouraged to pay close attention to work pieces that have slots or other surface profiles that may increase the risk of entanglement. They should keep clothing, jewelry and hair away from rotating and moving parts, as they may become caught.

  • Jewelry

  • No jewelry is allowed to be worn by any team members in technical or physically focused piano positions, including movers, refinishers, rebuilders, technicians or tuners. (Except for engagement/wedding rings)
  • Jewelry has the risk of getting caught in machinery with risk of team members getting injured.

  • Clothing

  • Supervisors are responsible for ensuring that all team members have no loose clothing
  • Rather than wearing a hoodie or coat in the shop over your uniform shirt, wear a fitted long sleeve undershirt or thermals under your uniform.

  • Hair (except admin)

  • Hair pulled back in bun, braid or ponytail (except admin)
  • Supervisors are responsible for ensuring that all team members have securely fastened their hair. Team members are required to pull back and protect long hair to prevent it from getting caught in machine parts such as belts, chain and rotating parts.

sections.title: DRESS CODE, GENERAL APPEARANCE & ATTITUDE
sections.html:
Please present yourself with a professional appearance, always ready to greet and welcome guests or to put customers at ease and excited to receive our services in their homes. You may also be included in a youtube video and or team/shop marketing photo images on any given day and looking sharp is always a plus for the whole team!

  • Hygiene

  • Shower daily and wear deodorant
  • Wear a BLP hat if hair is not clean

  • Hair & Grooming

  • All team members need to be well groomed & professionally presentable at all times.
  • Beards, mustaches and personal hairstyle choices need to be well groomed, styled and maintained.
  • Hair color choices need to be on the natural human hair color spectrum.

  • Tattoos

  • Please cover any tattoos with long sleeves and/or long pants during work hours.
  • Personal undershirts may be worn under the provided BLP work shirt uniform or ask an admin for a BLP shirt with long sleeves.
  • Undershirts must be black or dark gray
  • EXCEPTIONS: Team members with any visible existing tattoos, hired prior to July 1, 2023 are grandfathered in, to the standards of their former hire date, and may be exempt from this standard. If those team members continue to add additional visible tattoos, the standard may become required at the discretion of the owners.

  • Piercings

  • All visible body piercings need to be removed during work hours (except admin earrings)
  • Nose piercings should be adjusted to be non-visible if possible or else removed during work hours.
  • EXCEPTIONS: Team members with existing piercings, hired prior to July 1, 2023 are grandfathered in to be exempt from this standard. If those team members continue to add additional visible body piercings, the standard may become required for them at the discretion of the owners.

  • Uniform - Clothing Guidelines

**If you need a team shirt, please send a request to info@brighamlarsonpianos.com.

sections.title: WORK ENVIRONMENT
sections.html:
• Workspace

  • Keep the desk (admin) and/or workbench area clean and professional, always tour ready.
  • When working in the showroom be sure to be extra tidy. Keep tools neat and tables not set up in walking areas. We need to allow guests to be able to walk around safely.
  • If your project is longer than 1 day, tuck your tools, parts, and other materials under the piano at the end of your shift.
  • Ask admins to re-print wall signage once it gets worn, dirty or torn.

  • Language

  • Guests/Not Customers
  • When speaking to anyone visiting the piano store
  • Once they announce themselves as a buyer or customer... you can call them a customer
  • Colleagues/Not Competitors
  • For example, if you’re referring to Piano Gallery, don’t say they are our competitor, say they are our colleagues. We are not competing with them for business. We are challenging ourselves to elevate our product and our service to the highest level of consumer demand.
  • NEVER say ANYTHING negative to a guest about another business!!
  • No vulgar language or swearing.
  • Avoid slang and swearing substitute words (freekin’, etc.) and “teenage language”. Professionalism is first noticed with your appearance and then your speech, then your customer service.
  • Speak professionally and always calmly.

Communication

  • GroupMe
  • When posting to GroupME, use an all caps, one word intro to define the audience.
  • Examples: SHOP TEAM, ADMIN, EVERYONE, REFINISHERS, MOVERS, TUNERS, FIELD TECHS, ETC.
  • Problems
  • Text or talk to your direct supervisor
  • If the problem is with your supervisor, text or email BrighamLarsonPianos@gmail.com for help from Brigham (801) 830-0011 & Karmel (801) 427-9293
  • Admin Requests
  • Send admin requests for uniforms, clock in/out fixes, etc, to info@brighamlarsonpianos.com

SHOP STANDARD

sections.title: Cleanliness
sections.html:
• End of Day Exit

  • End tasks early enough to leave your desk or workspace clean and tidy and to perform closing checklist for your work area.
  • Shop Exit Checklist
  • Movers Exit Checklist
  • Refinishers Exit Checklist
  • Key Top Room Exit Checklist

  • Garbage Cans

  • Out of sight and hidden unless actively being used for a specific project.
  • Trash taken out immediately if visible above the rim of the can.
  • Always use liners.
  • Stowed under tables at the end of day for exit checklist and when not in use.

  • Dirty rags

  • Throw away into the TRASH, rags used with harsh chemicals, stain, wood chips or glue.
  • Dirty rags to WASH go into the corner bin in the tool area, under three shelves of clean rags.
  • Please DO NOT bring in cut up clothing to be used for rags.
  • If additional rags are needed, please report to the shop manager for more rags to be purchased or obtained.
  • When a full bag of rags are removed for washing, immediately replace the bin with a new trash bag before adding more dirty rags.

sections.title: Order
sections.html:
• Seating

  • Use only black padded shop stools for piano shop work seating.
  • Benches should NEVER be in the shop area. If a bench is in a shop area, take it immediately to a front desk admin for labeling and storage in the correct location.

  • Labels

  • Every piano should have a printed cardstock label
  • Use BLACK masking tape only and place labels on the right side of the piano.

  • Parts Room

  • Labeling Systems - coming soon
  • Supplies
  • Put supplies such as blue masking tape, sharpies and pencils back in their corresponding places after you’re finished using them. Do not leave blue masking tape, sharpies or pencils in the piano box upstairs in the cabinetry storage room

sections.title: Misc:
sections.html:
• Restoration Lines

  • Vertical mirrors are to be kept clear of tables and pianos. The entire mirror should always (preferably) be visible and ideally be aligned with rows between pianos.

  • Walkways

  • Keep the guest tour walkway (bathroom wall to pillars) free of parts, tools and trash cans so our guests have a clear, clean and orderly first impression.

  • Floors

  • Do not spend more than 1 minute vacuuming or sweeping. If it will take longer than that just leave it.
  • Floors will be swept and vacuumed by the facilities manager at the end of each day (except on Friday clean-up).
  • Anything bigger than a pinky nail should be picked up, swept up or vacuumed with a shop vac.
